summary: This is a clipped React documentation page for the useEffect Hook, which lets a component synchronize with an external system. It covers the signature useEffect(setup, dependencies?), how setup and cleanup run on mount, re-render and unmount, caveats such as Strict Mode double execution and useLayoutEffect for visual effects, and usage examples including custom Hooks, controlling a non-React widget, and fetching data with race-condition protection. Navigation menus and sandbox boilerplate were ignored.
one_line: React documentation for the useEffect Hook, covering its signature, cleanup behavior, caveats, and usage examples for syncing components with external systems.
key_facts: useEffect is a React Hook that lets you synchronize a component with an external system.
The signature of useEffect is useEffect(setup, dependencies?).
The setup function may optionally return a cleanup function.
When the component is added to the DOM, React runs the setup function.
After every re-render with changed dependencies, React first runs the cleanup function with the old values, then the setup function with the new values.
After the component is removed from the DOM, React runs the cleanup function.
The dependencies list is compared with Object.is, and it must have a constant number of items written inline like [dep1, dep2, dep3].
If the dependencies argument is omitted, the Effect re-runs after every re-render of the component.
When Strict Mode is on, React runs one extra development-only setup+cleanup cycle before the first real setup.
Effects only run on the client and do not run during server rendering.
If an Effect is doing something visual and the delay is noticeable, the page says to replace useEffect with useLayoutEffect.
The page states that useEffect is a Hook, so it can only be called at the top level of a component or custom Hook, not inside loops or conditions.
The page says that if you are not trying to synchronize with some external system, you probably don't need an Effect.
In the data fetching example, the ignore variable is initialized to false and set to true during cleanup to avoid race conditions.
